title: Praise — additional observations between intact explanations

scenes.title: 결과와 인정하는 반응 구별하기
lines: Watch the ball roll and the pins fall in Nintendo Switch Sports bowling.
The change in the pins is an outcome. We do not add a Strike label absent from this excerpt.
This is a starting point for separating an observable result from feeling that success was acknowledged.
In Hi-Fi RUSH, hit count, score and grading displays change after attacks.
Distinguish the increasing numbers from the brief Perfect response.
Even on one screen, a record display and acknowledgement of a particular action serve different purposes.
Ring Fit movement grades and a Switch Sports victory screen refer to different parts of play.
First identify whether the response marks one movement or the result of an entire match.
As in our earlier comparison, preserving reward rules while choosing what success to reveal makes the purpose clearer.

scenes.title: 동작 가까이에 반응 붙이기
lines: Watch the sequence of character movement and changing displays during Hi-Fi RUSH attacks.
We need to identify which attack a success response follows.
The beat indicator in the next excerpt guides a future movement; it alone does not mean success.
Separate the guidance from performance feedback and observe when an actual attack result appears.
Whether there is time to read the last result during continued play connects to our delay comparison.
We are observing movement and visible feedback at normal speed, with the source music muted.
Ring Fit guidance to hold a pose and the following grade also appear at different moments.
Hold and Return are movement instructions; Great and Good are performance feedback.
Do not treat guidance and praise as the same event merely because text appears in a similar place.

scenes.title: 어떤 행동을 인정하는가
lines: Hi-Fi RUSH combo attacks show both input guidance and actual hit results.
Follow the button instructions and acknowledgement of the attack separately.
The existence of an input does not prove that the movement succeeded.
When designing praise, first name the action: blocking, dodging or attack timing.
Ring Fit instructions to hold or slowly lower guide a pose.
Observe how their purpose differs from the subsequent Great grade.
Racket guidance in Switch Sports also tells us which direction to move.
Combat feedback follows a performed action; look at the connected event, beyond the wording.
Rewriting Good job to name the action can reveal what to change in your own game.

scenes.title: 작은 성공과 큰 마무리의 강도
lines: Hi-Fi RUSH presents continuing hits and large actions with different visual strengths.
While score and grade remain in the corner, the next attack continues in the center.
Observe whether a small success can be recognized without stopping for a long sequence.
Other combat excerpts also show brief hit responses and stronger attack effects.
These are not two experimental versions with equal scoring rules; they help identify each display role.
In a controlled comparison like our own, we can hold rules constant and change only response strength.
Ring Fit victory and level gains, and a Sports rank change, mark the end of longer intervals.
Separating movement grades from completion celebrations reduces the need to exaggerate every success.
Choose a response for one action, accumulated performance and the end of a larger interval.

scenes.title: 부분의 성공을 정직하게 다루기
lines: Some Hi-Fi RUSH combat excerpts show a lower grade; observe it with the actual movement.
Another scene shows Perfect after a movement at a device; it grades that particular action.
Not extending one success into a claim of perfect overall play connects to honest acknowledgement.
An ability-state menu and a combat grade are different; state information is not praise itself.
Record the visible hit and grade without inventing an unseen failure or completion condition.
What we acknowledge during a failure should be based on an action that actually succeeded.
Ring Fit movement and collection display the acquired item; record only the observed action.
The following traversal alone does not prove a perfect completion of the entire stage.
Together with our earlier failure comparison, check what a truthful small acknowledgement would be.

scenes.title: 반응과 다음 행동을 함께 보기
lines: Hi-Fi RUSH combat shows moving enemies and the character alongside corner status displays.
Observe whether feedback can be noticed while the next target and danger remain readable.
Avoiding obstruction when making a response larger connects to our earlier placement comparison.
In other combat and sports scenes, examine the center, corners and movement direction separately.
Seeing a message briefly is not proof that a person playing understood it.
During continued movement, such as Ring Fit traversal, also consider the next object to look at.
In the final minigames, observe where scores and responses such as Nice appear after real movements.
Turn this into a question for a person: can they recognize both the action and result on a small screen?
Use real action scenes with timing, specificity, strength, honesty and placement to design praise.
